## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

load(url(
  "https://github.com/GarciaRios/govt_3990/raw/gh-pages/Labs/lab6/acs.RData"
))

source(url(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GarciaRios/govt_3990/gh-pages/Labs/lab7/plot_ss.R"
))

acs_emp <- acs |>
  filter(
    employment == "employed",
    income > 0,
    !is.na(hrs_work)
  )
```

# Exercises

## Exercise 1: Scatterplot and correlation

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_emp,
  aes(x = hrs_work, y = income)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  labs(
    x = "Hours worked per week",
    y = "Annual income ($)",
    title = "Annual income and weekly hours worked"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Describe the form, direction, strength, and unusual observations.

> 

Does a straight line seem like a useful summary?

> 

```{r}
acs_emp |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(hrs_work, income)
  )
```

Interpret the correlation.

> 

## Exercise 2: Residuals

Create the demonstration sample:

```{r}
set.seed(311)

acs_demo <- acs_emp |>
  slice_sample(n = 50)
```

Run this interactively in the Console:

```{r}
#| eval: false
plot_ss(
  x = hrs_work,
  y = income,
  data = acs_demo
)
```

What does a positive residual mean? What does a negative residual mean?

> 

## Exercise 3: Sum of squared residuals

Run this interactively several times:

```{r}
#| eval: false
plot_ss(
  x = hrs_work,
  y = income,
  data = acs_demo,
  showSquares = TRUE
)
```

What is the smallest sum of squares you obtain?

> 

How does your line compare with someone sitting near you?

> 

## Exercise 4: The linear model

```{r}
income_hours_model <- lm(
  income ~ hrs_work,
  data = acs_emp
)

summary(income_hours_model)
```

Write the fitted regression equation.

> 

Interpret the slope.

> 

Interpret the intercept. Is it substantively meaningful?

> 

## Exercise 5: (R^2)

Report and interpret \(R^2\).

> 

How does \(R^2\) relate to the correlation from Exercise 1?

> 

## Exercise 6: Compare another predictor

```{r}
income_age_model <- lm(
  income ~ age,
  data = acs_emp
)

summary(income_age_model)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_emp,
  aes(x = age, y = income)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Write the fitted equation and interpret the slope.

> 

Report \(R^2\).

> 

Which variable accounts for more variation in income: `hrs_work` or `age`?

> 

Does a straight line look equally appropriate for both relationships?

> 

## Exercise 7: Prediction and residual

Predict income for someone working 40 hours per week:

```{r}
predict(
  income_hours_model,
  newdata = data.frame(
    hrs_work = 40
  )
)
```

Select one observed respondent working 40 hours:

```{r}
example_worker <- acs_emp |>
  filter(hrs_work == 40) |>
  slice(1)

example_prediction <- predict(
  income_hours_model,
  newdata = example_worker
)

example_worker |>
  transmute(
    hrs_work,
    income,
    predicted_income = as.numeric(example_prediction),
    residual = income - as.numeric(example_prediction)
  )
```

What is the residual? Did the model overpredict or underpredict income?

> 

## Exercise 8: Residual plot

```{r}
model_check <- tibble(
  fitted = fitted(income_hours_model),
  residual = resid(income_hours_model)
)

ggplot(
  model_check,
  aes(x = fitted, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Is there an obvious pattern?

> 

Does the residual spread remain roughly constant?

> 

## Exercise 9: Residual distribution

```{r}
ggplot(
  model_check,
  aes(x = residual)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Do the residuals appear approximately normal?

> 

What does this suggest about the limitations of the model?

>
